title: Geofenced throughput contracts and scheduled evacuation windows for multi-zone dedicated fleets
creator: Mariana Ortiz
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated pools in regulated regions need predictable throughput guarantees and a predictable failover/evacuation behavior that respects data residency constraints. Current placement and autoscaling primitives do not provide an operator-friendly way to: 1) reserve throughput for a customer across a region while still allowing soft spillover under capacity pressure; 2) schedule controlled evacuation windows per zone for maintenance while avoiding simultaneous cross-zone impact; 3) attach immutable data-residency tags that prevent accidental cross-region spillover during emergency failovers.

Goal: Implement a three-part feature set: (A) geofenced throughput contracts that reserve a minimum token throughput per customer per region with configurable spillover policies, (B) scheduled evacuation windows and staggered drains at the fleet-or-zone level with safety-wideband constraints, and (C) residency-lock metadata enforced in the placement/orchestrator layer to block non-compliant failovers. This ticket covers design, core runtime changes, API surfaces, and initial rollout automation for one pilot customer and two regions (eu-west-1, us-west-2).
acceptance_criteria: Throughput contract API: create/update/delete contracts that reserve N rps or token-rate for a dedicated pool region and surface current reservation usage in Console

Spillover policy: administrative config supports 'hard' (no spillover), 'soft' (best-effort spillover with throttled degradation), and 'elastic' (allow full spillover with cost-metric routing), and is enforced by orchestrator during allocation/failover
Evacuation scheduling: operator can schedule a drain window for a given zone with a stagger offset (minutes) and the runtime performs graceful handoff with KV-cache sync and prewarm where needed
Residency locking: placement controller rejects placement targets that would move data outside allowed residency tags; audits emitted to logging and Console
Safe-failover tests: chaos simulation shows no customer experiences >3x expected tail latency or >20% throughput loss for more than 5 minutes during scheduled drains in the pilot
Console: route-level visuals show reservation utilization, upcoming evacuation windows, and any active residency violations
Feature-flagged rollout: feature can be toggled per-account and region for staged release
technical_notes:
High level architecture: add a 'throughput_contract' resource to pool metadata persisted in config-store. Orchestrator scheduler will consult contracts when placing requests and when making preemption decisions. Introduce a 'reserve bucket' accounting model: each contract maps to a rate-limited token bucket evaluated at scheduling time. Spillover decision is policy-led: 'hard' returns 429 when contract exhausted; 'soft' routes to compatible variants with degraded throughput SLAs; 'elastic' permits routing but records cost tags. Evacuation scheduling leverages existing drain APIs but adds 'stagger' and 'prewarm' hooks: we must drain replicas sequentially with a configurable overlap to allow KV cache replication and model rewarm. Residency locking implemented as an admission check in the placement controller; use signed residency assertions on the pool to prevent bypass. Persistence: store contracts and evacuation schedules in the cluster config-store with versioned schema v1.

Implementation constraints: do not increase p99 latency by >5% under baseline load. Modifications to hot path must be minimal; prefer sidecar admission checks or pre-scheduler evaluation stage. Ensure RBAC checks for contract creation (only platform admins + account managers).
implementation_plan: Design review and finalize API models (1 week) — deliver OpenAPI spec and Console mockups
Scheduler: implement read-only contract checks and token-bucket accounting (2 weeks) behind FF
Placement controller: enforce residency locks and add audit events (1 week)
Drain/evac: extend drain service with stagger + prewarm hooks and KV sync endpoints (2 weeks)
Console: surface reservation utilization and schedule editor (2 weeks)
Integration: QA pilot with one customer in eu-west-1 and us-west-2, run chaos schedule tests (1 week)
Rollout: enable for pilot customers behind FF, monitor SLOs, iterate on throttling logic
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket accounting, e2e tests for scheduled drains (simulate KV cache warmup and request replay), chaos testing to simulate zone failure during active evacuation windows, load test to validate latency and throughput under 'soft' and 'elastic' spillover policies. Add regression checks to CI to ensure placement admits no cross-residency placements when residency lock present.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated in staging: enable on internal dedicated clusters, run synthetic traffic against reserved contracts
Canary: enable for 2 pilot customers in eu-west-1 and us-west-2, observe for 7 days
Gradual: expand to customers who opt-in in controlled cohorts; enable console UI to request ramp
GA: after 3 customer pilots and SLO validation, flip default FF to on for Dedicated customers with a migration path
